parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is a restrictive national framework (passport markers forced to sex assigned at birth, X markers halted, entry-refusal and fraud-ineligibility instructions for document discrepancies, transgender athlete entry ban, custody abuses) plus a state layer among the most restrictive: facility bans in state-owned settings, closed birth-certificate markers, criminal misdemeanor for facility trespass after refusal to depart, and a documented arrest precedent elsewhere under an identical law. Courts partially contest national measures but the state court has extended restriction retroactively. No state-specific traveler violence is documented, and imprisonment is not the typical outcome; severity is moderate-to-major, frequency high via universal document/facility exposure. Care access for adults exists only privately. This sits in the Elevated band.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport/sex-marker regime, entry-refusal and fraud-ineligibility instructions for discrepancies, trans athlete ban; passport confiscations reported nationally.
entry_documents.protection: Litigation ongoing; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic; existing X passports remain valid until expiration.
entry_documents.interaction: State document rules compound the national regime for any internal ID checks.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policies described as conversion therapy; immigration custody forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse of trans men; trespass arrest precedent (24h men's ward holding) in a neighbouring state.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute; some orders enjoined.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A bathroom encounter can escalate from a request to leave to arrest and jail within state-owned buildings.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State facility bans (K-12 and state-owned settings via executive order covering shelters, crisis centres, incarceration); misdemeanor trespass with documented arrest under a similar statute in another state.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass trigger requires refusal to depart when asked; exemptions exist.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State definitions override identity for all state agency purposes, including incarceration placement.

care_services.exposure: State law bars public funds/facilities and Medicaid for gender-affirming care for minors and adults (criminal misdemeanor for employees); care only via private facilities at private cost; minor travelling with guardian cannot access affirming care in public settings.
care_services.protection: Exemptions for emergency treatment to prevent death or major impairment, complications, and mental-health counseling.
care_services.interaction: Federal rules proposed to bar public insurance reimbursement for minors compound the state ban.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State executive order defines sex biologically for all state purposes; national counterterrorism language targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; state hate-crime law excludes gender identity; no state discrimination protection.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National 2020 employment ruling and national hate-crime statute remain on paper and were formally ordered 'corrected' by the 2025 executive order, weakening them as recourse.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile official framing licenses social and administrative hostility.

minors_guardians.exposure: Total ban on affirming care for minors statewide; K-12 facility bans; school outing/prosecution dynamics from national orders; a trans minor resident died after a school bathroom assault.
minors_guardians.protection: Emergency-care exemption; one city's local anti-discrimination ordinance.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling parent risks investigation exposure if a minor's transition becomes known to schools or officials.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented resident-level hostility: death threats to a 12-year-old (2018), Nex Benedict beating/death (2024); police response not shown protective; no state traveler-violence incident documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime prosecution available in federal court.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police interaction risks outing via ID checks; state law offers no bias recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: State supreme court retroactively voided even cisgender marker corrections; no state legal gender recognition; driver's licence marker status unknown; pending HB 1225 would harden closure.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active national litigation and legal-aid FAQ; several federal orders enjoined; state tracker maps help travellers plan.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow, contested, and state-level relief is effectively absent.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A is a universal state registration/exclusion regime with near-certain enforcement. Here the sharpest universal measure (passport sex markers, entry-refusal instructions) is comparable in exposure breadth, but enforcement is contested in court, fraud findings are not automatic, and no systematic border exclusion of trans visitors is documented; hence materially above 0.35-A.

0.55-B is discretionary secondary screening with administrative outcomes. This jurisdiction's border regime is more adversarial (fraud-ineligibility instructions, athlete entry ban), and the state adds facility criminalisation and care denial, so it sits below 0.55-B; but outcomes are likewise mostly administrative and courts partly function.

0.75-C features trained officers, tribunal appeals, and brief-detention norms. This jurisdiction lacks state anti-discrimination law, has a documented trespass arrest precedent, closed state document corrections, and a state supreme court extending restriction — well below 0.75-C.

0.45-D is durable universal exposure via registration/database with harassment and eviction as typical harms and no credible lethality. This regime is similar: universal document/facility exposure, typical harms of exclusion, arrest possibility, care denial — but with some contested courts and no state targeting sweeps, placing it around 0.45-D, slightly below its midpoint toward the lower 40s.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime couples a hostile national document and entry framework — passport markers fixed at birth sex, X markers halted, entry-referral and fraud instructions, custody abuses — with a state layer among the most restrictive: universal biologically-defined sex for state purposes, facility bans, criminal misdemeanor facility trespass with a documented arrest elsewhere under identical law, closed gender-marker changes retroactively, and near-total public care bans for minors and adults. Courts partially check the national layer, and no state-specific violence against visitors is documented, keeping this above the 0.35 exclusion tier. But the exposures are universal (every ID check, every state-owned facility, any care need), remedies within the state are absent, and the state adds its own hostile layer to the parent — so the score sits in the Elevated band, below the 0.55 midpoint.
